findings.trigger: A retest for a container finishes without success (either all 3 probes over ~2 minutes fail, or _attempts() raises and is caught at :629) and the subsequent cleanup call `support.set_testing(container_name, False)` at :635 itself raises (e.g. the support-verdicts file cannot be written). The bare `except Exception: pass` at :636-637 swallows that error. The 'testing' flag for that container is then never cleared, so `game_query_support_status` (polled by the UI) reports `testing: true` forever even though the test has already ended - the spinner never resolves until an unrelated later retest happens to succeed in clearing it.
findings.suggestion: Log the exception from the cleanup `support.set_testing(...)` call (at least at ERROR/WARNING) instead of a bare pass, so a stuck spinner is at least visible in the logs, matching the Z8 pattern already fixed elsewhere for similar cleanup-after-failure code.

findings.trigger: POST /api/simulate-donation-broadcast is called (e.g. by an admin testing the donation broadcast feature). The handler does nothing except log a line and immediately returns `{'success': True, 'message': 'Donation broadcast simulation not yet implemented'}` - no broadcast, no simulation, nothing was actually done, yet `success` is `True`.
findings.suggestion: Return `success: False` (or a distinct status such as 'not_implemented') for a stub endpoint, so a caller that only checks the `success` flag cannot mistake 'nothing happened' for 'the simulated broadcast worked' - this is the exact pattern Z3 was written against.

findings.trigger: In `update_task_status` (:181), `delete_task_route` (:219) and both branches of `edit_task_route` (:262 GET, :290 PUT), the failure path does `status_code = 404 if "not found" in result.error.lower() else ...` directly on `result.error`. If the underlying TaskManagementService ever returns `success=False` with `error=None` (no message set), `.lower()` raises `AttributeError`, which is caught by each function's own `except (ImportError, AttributeError, RuntimeError)` clause and turned into a generic 'Service error ...' 500 response instead of the correct 400/404 with the service's real error text.
findings.suggestion: Guard with `(result.error or '')` before `.lower()` in all four call sites so a missing error message degrades to the intended 400/404 branch instead of a misleading 500.
findings.unsure_why: The service layer (services/web/task_management_service.py) that produces `result` is not in this section, so it cannot be confirmed whether it guarantees a non-None string in `error` whenever `success` is False. If it always sets `error`, this code path never triggers. Even when it does trigger, the failure is still visible to the caller (a 500 with an error body), not silent.

notes: app/blueprints/main_routes.py:27-85 (_get_cached_mech_state) is not called anywhere in this file; its two nested compat classes (the two PLAN entries at :40 and :62) are currently field-for-field identical in shape and show no divergence today, so no finding - noted only because the task highlighted 'two places that do the same thing and may drift apart', and because a helper with no visible caller inside this section could be genuinely dead code reachable only from files outside this section (e.g. a template or another blueprint), which cannot be verified from here. app/blueprints/main_routes.py:289 (enable_temp_debug) reads `duration_minutes = request.form.get('duration', 10)`, which yields a string when the form field is present and an int only when it is absent; this inconsistency is passed straight into DebugModeRequest without casting. Whether this matters depends entirely on services/web/diagnostics_service.py (out of scope for this section); if it mishandles a string, the existing (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError) handler already turns it into a visible 400, so it was not raised as a formal finding. All three files in this section are thin Flask-blueprint wrappers around service objects that live outside this section (services/web/*, services/donation/*, services/infrastructure/*, services/mech/*); most of the actual business logic, and therefore most of the guarantees in SPEC.md (Z1, Z2, Z4, Z6, Z7, Z9, Z10), cannot be judged from this section alone - only Z3/Z8-style 'reported success without doing the work' and 'silent failure' patterns are visible at this layer, which is where F1-F3 come from.
